audience.programmeDescription: Use living cells and microorganisms to make useful products. Wageningen Biotechnology combines molecular biology, microbiology and biochemistry with chemistry, mathematics, biological production and process design.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programme develops related molecular, experimental and quantitative interests, with medical applications and attention to production impacts. Specialist industrial bioprocess study remains a substantial difference.

notes.text: The UCR programme offers related molecular, laboratory and quantitative study. It does not reproduce Wageningen’s dedicated chemistry, industrial microbiology, cell-factory, bioreactor and separation-design sequence or its required 24-credit thesis. Optional UCR research is additional to the 180-credit schedule.

selectedDescriptions.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedDescriptions.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedDescriptions.name: Consumer Product Design
selectedDescriptions.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

selectedDescriptions.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
selectedDescriptions.text: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

selectedDescriptions.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
selectedDescriptions.text: Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python, Keras and TensorFlow implementations. Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

selectedDescriptions.name: Linear Algebra
selectedDescriptions.text: Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine eigenvalues, orthogonality, least-squares approximation, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis, with Mathematica supporting analytical problem-solving.

selectedDescriptions.name: Environmental Biogeochemistry
selectedDescriptions.text: Examines chemical and biological controls on interactions among water, minerals, rocks and soils. Topics include equilibrium, speciation, redox chemistry, adsorption, weathering and biomineralisation. Laboratory work, geochemical modelling and an environmental project connect these processes to contaminant behaviour, wastewater treatment, remediation and resource recovery.

A laboratory project makes and tests starch-based biopolymers.

selectedDescriptions.text: Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. Students connect anatomy and physiology with symptoms, disease mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis across digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine and nervous systems. Clinical cases and an imaginary-disease assignment develop coherent pathophysiological explanations.
